verses.79:2: Vós que {regis}, atendei: * vós que {deducis} José como ovelha.
verses.79:2b: Vós que estais sentado sobre os querubins, * {manifestare} diante de Efraim, Benjamim e Manassés.
verses.79:5: Senhor, {virt5}, * até quando estareis irado {super} a oração do vosso servo?
verses.79:6: Com pão de lágrimas {cibabis}: * e nos dareis de beber em lágrimas, {mensura}?
verses.79:7: Fizestes de nós {contradictio} os nossos vizinhos: * e os nossos inimigos zombaram de nós.
verses.79:9: Transportastes do Egito uma vinha: * {ejecisti} as nações, e a plantastes.
verses.79:10: Fostes guia do caminho {conspectu}: * plantastes as suas raízes, e ela encheu a terra.
verses.79:11: A sua sombra cobriu os montes: * e {arbusta} os cedros de Deus.
verses.79:12: Estendeu os seus sarmentos até o mar: * e até o rio os seus rebentos.
verses.79:13: Por que destruístes a sua cerca: * e todos os que passam pelo caminho a {vindemiant}?
verses.79:15: {virt15}, voltai-vos: * olhai do céu, e vede, e visitai esta vinha.
verses.79:16: E {perfice} aquela que a vossa direita plantou: * e sobre o filho do homem, {confirm16}.
verses.79:17: {incensa}, * à repreensão do vosso rosto perecerão.
verses.79:18: {fiat} a vossa mão sobre o homem da vossa direita: * e sobre o filho do homem, {confirm18}.
verses.79:19: E de vós {discedimus}, {vivificabis}: * e invocaremos o vosso nome.

decisions.why: The refrain's verb, three times, identical in the three places as the Latin is. The *convértere* row gives *voltar*, but names this very phrase as a test, and D25's exception (*converter* where men turn to God) was extended to God as the one who turns souls: 18:8 *convértens ánimas* → *converte as almas*, 22:2 *ánimam meam convértit* → *converteu a minha alma*. Here God is asked to turn *us*; ἐπίστρεψον ἡμᾶς holds both 'turn us back' (restore) and 'turn us to you', and *convertei-nos* holds both as well, the religious sense first — which is how the Church has prayed this refrain (and 84:5 *Convérte nos, Deus*, at Compline). DRB 'convert us'; MS1932 *converte-nos* at 79:4 and 79:20. The cost: 79:15 *Deus virtútum, convértere* is the formula *Voltai-vos* (row), so the Latin's one root in the refrain and in 79:15 becomes two Portuguese verbs. *fazei-nos voltar* keeps that echo but is heavier and reads as 'bring us back (home)'. *Convertei* is safe under rule 3 (past *converti*).

options.label: convertei-nos
options.note: Ruling: D25's exception as applied at 18:8, 22:2; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: fazei-nos voltar
options.note: the row's *voltar*, causative as 52:7 *fizer voltar*; keeps the echo with 79:15 *voltai-vos*; two syllables longer.

options.label: restaurai-nos
options.note: MS1932 at 79:8 only; the Hebrew's sense (hashivenu), says less than the Latin's turning.

decisions.why: The Latin has no indirect object (ἐπίφανον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου, 'make your face shine forth'). DRB supplies 'us' at 79:4 but not at 79:8, MS1932 supplies *-nos* in all three. Not supplied: the refrain is the same three times in the Latin and stays so; *mostrai a vossa face* is complete Portuguese. *fácies → face* (row), apart from *vultus → rosto* (79:17). *mostrai* is safe (past *mostrei*).

options.label: fazei brilhar a vossa face
options.note: the Greek's and the Hebrew's image; not the Latin's verb.

decisions.why: D43: *Dóminus virtútum → o Senhor dos poderes*; 58:6 *Dómine, Deus virtútum → Senhor, Deus dos poderes*. The four places grow in the Latin (*Deus* 79:4 → *Deus virtútum* 79:8, 79:15 → *Dómine, Deus virtútum* 79:20, and 79:5), and the Portuguese grows the same way. D43 is flagged for Gustavo: *dos exércitos* (MS1932, DRB 'hosts') is the Hebrew's Sabaoth. One touch changes all four.

The *régere* row foresaw this verse ('79:2 *Qui regis Israël* will follow'; 22:1 *O Senhor me rege*). The Greek is ὁ ποιμαίνων, 'you who shepherd', and the next colon's sheep carries that image; but the Latin says *regis*, and 22:1 kept *reger* against the familiar shepherd for the same reason. The ambiguity reader of Ps 27 did not know *regei-os*; *regeis* is the same verb.

options.label: apascentais Israel
options.note: the Greek's ποιμαίνων; not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: D22: *dedúcere* of guidance → *guiar* (ὁ ὁδηγῶν); 76:21 *Deduxísti sicut oves pópulum tuum* → *Guiastes o vosso povo como ovelhas* has the same image. *velut ovem* is singular in the Latin (the Greek has the plural πρόβατα): *como ovelha*, without the article, as 76:21 *como ovelhas* (MS1932 *como uma ovelha*, a syllable longer). Natural order puts the object before the comparison.

options.label: conduzis
options.note: MS1932; the cognate (not an imperative here, so rule 3 does not bar it).

decisions.why: A passive imperative, 'show yourself' (ἐμφάνηθι, 'appear'). The reflexive cognate says it exactly, and keeps it apart from *osténde → mostrai* two verses on. DRB 'shine forth', MS1932 *manifesta-te*. Safe under rule 3 (past *manifestei*).

options.label: mostrai-vos
options.note: plainer; merges with *osténde* in the refrain.

options.label: aparecei
options.note: the Greek's sense; loses the Latin's root.

decisions.why: *excitáre* is 'rouse, wake up' (ἐξέγειρον), the image of a power that sleeps; *despertai* keeps it and is safe (past *despertei*). *poténtia → potência* follows the open row (64:7, 70:19 *A vossa potência*); *poder* is *virtus*'s, and *virtútum* stands two verses later. MS1932 *Mostra o teu poder* loses the waking.

*salvum fácere → salvar* (row). The purpose clause is kept finite, as the Latin's subjunctive is; it also sits within a syllable of the Latin colon. *para nos salvar* (DRB 'to save us') is shorter by two.

*irásci super* is anger directed at (ἐπί + acc.); *irar-se sobre* is not Portuguese. 73:1 *irátus est furor tuus super oves* → *se irou o vosso furor contra as ovelhas* sets the precedent; DRB 'angry against'. MS1932 *sem ouvir a oração* paraphrases.

options.label: diante de
options.note: softer; the anger in the presence of the prayer.

decisions.why: Two futures that DRB and MS1932 both read as a continuation of 79:5's 'how long'; DO's Latin ends the verse with a question mark, and so does the Portuguese — no *até quando* supplied (MS1932 supplies it in parentheses). *cibáre* 'to feed' → *alimentar*. The bread is put first so that the colon ends on a stressed verb rather than on the proparoxytone *lágrimas*, and so that the verse does not open on a clitic.

decisions.latin: et potum dabis nobis in lácrimis in mensúra?
decisions.why: *in mensúra* (ἐν μέτρῳ): drink measured out, which may be rationed or full — the Latin does not say which. *por medida* is the plain Portuguese for 'by measure' and leaves that open; *com medida* would say 'sparingly', MS1932's *com abundância* is the Hebrew's 'a third-measure' read as plenty. *in lácrimis* 'in tears' is taken as the drink itself (DRB 'give us for our drink tears'), which *dar a beber lágrimas* says without the ambiguous *em lágrimas* ('while weeping').

decisions.latin: Posuísti nos in contradictiónem vicínis nostris
decisions.why: *contradíctio → contenda* (row: the blind reader heard *contradições* as inconsistencies at 17:44). *Posuísti nos* + predicate is built as 43:14 *Fizestes de nós uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos* (the same verb, the same neighbours). We are made a thing our neighbours dispute over (ἀντιλογία); DRB 'a contradiction to our neighbours', MS1932 *um objecto de disputa para*.

options.label: contenda para
options.note: Ruling: the row; the 43:14 build without the article (stylist v1: *uma contenda* sounds like one quarrel handed over).

options.label: uma contenda para
options.note: draft 1; the 43:14 build to the letter.

decisions.why: *ejícere* 'cast out' (ἐξέβαλες) → *lançar fora* (MS1932), kept apart from *expéllere → expulsar* (43:3 *et expulísti eos → e os expulsastes*, the same story of the conquest).

decisions.latin: Dux itíneris fuísti in conspéctu ejus
decisions.why: *in conspéctu* + genitive → *à vista de* (the *conspéctus* row's proposal, tried on 5:9, 22:5, 55:9). Here the Greek is ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῆς 'before it', which *diante dela* (MS1932) says more plainly; kept to the row so that the 51 places stay one. *dux → guia* (row), *iter → caminho* (row).

options.label: diante dela
options.note: Ruling in draft 2: the stylist (v1) heard *à vista* first as "in cash" and the phrase as bureaucratic; the ambiguity reader lost the link of *dela* to the vine. The Greek is ἔμπροσθεν, "before"; MS1932 *diante dela*. A local departure from the conspéctus row, recorded there.

decisions.why: *arbústa* are the trees a vine is trained on (L&S; Greek ἀναδενδράδες, 'vines climbing trees'); here the vine's upper growth that covered the cedars. The verb is carried over from the first colon, as the Latin does: a comma marks the ellipsis. Three growth words follow in 79:11–12 (*arbústa, pálmites, propágines*) and each keeps its own: *ramos, sarmentos, rebentos* (MS1932 has *sarmentos, ramagem, rebentos*). Draft 2: the Latinist (v1) held *ramos* to narrow *arbústa* (trees, a planted grove) and to blur it with *pálmites*; *arvoredo* taken. The ambiguity reader heard the verbless colon as apposition (*its branches were the cedars of God*); the gapped verb is supplied, as grammar (D2): *e o seu arvoredo cobriu os cedros de Deus* would repeat *cobriu*; *e o seu arvoredo, os cedros de Deus* keeps the ellipsis but is misheard. Supplied as *cobriu* in the slot so the whole choice is one touch.

options.label: o seu arvoredo cobriu
options.note: Ruling in draft 2: the Latinist's noun; the verb of the first colon supplied against the misheard apposition.

options.label: as suas ramagens
options.note: collective; closer to the Latin's plural of growth.

options.label: o seu arvoredo, (ellipsis)
options.note: the Latinist's fix to the letter; keeps the Latin's ellipsis, heard as apposition.

decisions.why: *vindemiáre* is to gather the grapes (τρυγῶσιν); *vindimar* is the one word for it, and MS1932's. The ambiguity reader is asked whether it is understood; *colhem as suas uvas* explains it in three words.

options.label: vindimam
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's one word; MS1932.

options.label: colhem as uvas
options.note: plainer; drops the pronoun *eam* into *as uvas*.

decisions.why: In church Latin *extermináre* is to destroy, lay waste (L&S; DRB 'hath laid it waste'); the Greek here is ἐλυμήνατο, 'ravaged'. 43:3 has *extermináre* of nations (ἐξωλέθρευσεν) → *exterminou*; D15's test lets two Greek verbs part, and a vine is ravaged rather than exterminated. *silva → selva* (D44).

*singuláris ferus* is the wild beast that lives alone (μονιὸς ἄγριος; the solitary boar of the first colon, or another beast — the Latin does not say). *solitária* says it; DRB's calque 'a singular wild beast' would be heard as 'remarkable'; MS1932 *a fera selvagem* drops *singuláris*.

D43: *depáscere → pastar* (48:15 *a morte os pastará*). The Greek κατενεμήσατο is 'grazed it down', which is exactly *pastar* with an object. *devorou* (MS1932, DRB) is the stronger, freer word. Draft 2: the stylist's order *e pastou-a a fera solitária* (v1): it answers *Devastou-a* in the first colon and removes the *a … a* of article and clitic. Order only (D2).

*perfícere → aperfeiçoar* (row, which tried *aperfeiçoai* on this verse; safe, past *aperfeiçoei*). κατάρτισαι is 'make whole, restore', which *aperfeiçoar* covers. *eam, quam* → *aquela que*: the vine, not named, as in the Latin. MS1932 *Protege* paraphrases.

options.label: restaurai
options.note: the Greek's sense; not the Latin's verb.

decisions.why: The same colon twice, identical. *confirmáre* with a person as object → *firmar* (the row's proposal, 37:3, 40:13, 50:14, 70:6); the Greek is ἐκραταίωσας σεαυτῷ, 'made strong for yourself'. *confirmastes* would be heard as attesting (36:17). The ellipsis *e sobre o filho do homem* (79:16) is the Latin's own, left as it is. *fílius hóminis* lowercase (row).

options.label: que fortalecestes para vós
options.note: the Greek's 'strengthened'; MS1932's option in the row.

decisions.why: *incénsa … suffóssa* can be feminine singular (the vine) or neuter plural ('things set on fire', DRB). The Greek has the feminine singular (ἐμπεπυρισμένη … ἀνεσκαμμένη) and MS1932 reads the vine; Portuguese must choose a gender, and the Greek decides it. *perecerão* stays plural with no subject named, as *períbunt* — the vine's burners or the vine's people; the Latin does not say. *suffódere* 'dig under' (L&S; ἀνεσκαμμένη 'dug up'): *escavada*; MS1932 *arrancada* interprets.

options.label: Queimada a fogo, e escavada
options.note: Ruling: the vine, as the Greek.

options.label: As coisas queimadas a fogo, e escavadas

forms.incensa: As coisas queimadas a fogo, e escavadas

decisions.why: The Latin is present, *discédimus* (the Greek's οὐ μὴ ἀποστῶμεν is an emphatic future); DRB keeps the present 'we depart not', MS1932 makes it a future with *Então*. Kept present, as the Latin. *discédere a → afastar-se de* (row).

*vivificáre → vivificar* (row; 118, 40:3, 70:20). The subject *vós* is named so that the clitic has a word before it; *de vós, vós* makes a turn from 'we' to 'you' that the Latin makes by the verb ending. The mesóclise *vivificar-nos-eis* avoids the repetition but is heavy. Draft 2: the stylist (v1) heard *de vós, vós* as a stammer; the first colon is reordered *E de vós não nos afastamos*, so the two pronouns are no longer side by side (order only). His *nos vivificareis* (clitic opening the clause) is not written Portuguese; the mesóclise stays an option.

options.label: vós nos dareis a vida
options.note: MS1932 *tu nos darás a vida*; the row's option.

decisions.why: The *fíeri* row: jussive *Fiat* → *Seja* (118:173 *Seja a vossa mão para me salvar*, held twice against the stylist). The stylist (v1) called *Seja … sobre* a calque and asked *Esteja*: that turns a becoming into a state, which *fíeri* is not. Held; *Esteja* one touch away.

choices.79:2: *inténde → atendei* (D3), absolute as the Latin. The anaphora *Qui … qui … Qui* (79:2, 2b) is said *Vós que* three times: the named subject lets each relative clause be heard as said to God.
choices.79:2b: *sedes super Chérubim → estais sentado sobre os querubins* (as 46:9 *está sentado sobre*); first colon +3 syllables over the Latin, accepted: the state 'seated' needs the auxiliary. *coram → diante de*. The Latin's *et* before *Manásse* kept.
choices.79:4: The refrain, first form. 79:8 and 79:20 are built from the same slots; only the title grows, as in the Latin.
choices.79:5: *quoúsque → até quando* (as *úsquequo*). Draft 2: *irascéris* → *estareis irado* (the stylist, v1: *vos irareis* is a knot of r's), the future said as copula + participle — grammar (D2), the verb's root kept. *servus → servo* (row).
choices.79:6: *pane lacrimárum → pão de lágrimas*, singular, as the Latin. Draft 2: *in lácrimis* kept as a prepositional phrase with *dar de beber* for *potum dare* (the Latinist, v1): *e nos dareis de beber em lágrimas* — the drink that is tears, or given while weeping; the Latin's *in* holds both.
choices.79:9: *transférre → transportar* (D43). *víneam* without an article in Latin: *uma vinha* (DRB 'a vineyard'); put at the end of the colon, the natural place for the new thing.
choices.79:10: Draft 2: the subject *ela* named (the stylist, v1; the ambiguity reader heard God first): *implévit* is singular, so it is the vine, not the roots or God. *dux → guia*, *iter → caminho* (rows).
choices.79:11: Natural order: *A sua sombra cobriu os montes* (the Latin has the verb first).
choices.79:12: *pálmites → sarmentos*, *propágines → rebentos* (MS1932 for the second). *usque ad → até*.
choices.79:13: *Ut quid → Por que* (as 73:1). *macéria → cerca* (row, 61:4). Draft 2: the stylist's order (v1), the subject before the verb, so that *e a vindimam* is not heard as *e à vindima* and the pronoun is no longer next to *cerca*.
choices.79:15: *Convértere* with God as subject → *Voltai-vos* (formula row; 6:5). *réspice → olhai*; *vísita → visitai* (row).
choices.79:17: *igni → a fogo*. Singular participles and a plural verb with no subject: the Latin's (*incénsa … períbunt*). The stylist asked a colon at the mark to let the plural begin a new thought (refused: it makes the participles a sentence of their own, MS1932's reading, where the Latin runs on). *ab increpatióne → à repreensão* (formula row); *vultus → rosto* (row).
choices.79:18: *Fiat manus tua → Seja a vossa mão* (the *fíeri* row, as 118:173). *vir déxteræ tuæ → o homem da vossa direita*; *déxtera → direita* (row).
choices.79:19: *invocáre → invocar* (row). Natural order: *e invocaremos o vosso nome*.
choices.79:20: The refrain with its fullest title, *Senhor, Deus dos poderes*, = 79:5's address.
choices.79:14: The Latin's order, verb first, in both colons: *Devastou-a … e pastou-a* (draft 1's *O javali da selva a devastou … a pastou* rhymed at both cadences; draft 2 takes the stylist's order in the second colon). *silva → selva* (D44).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps079.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no DM1962 for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D2, D3 (*atender*), D5 n/a, D22 (*guiar*), D25 (*converter* for God turning men), D43 (*Deus dos poderes*, *transportar*, *pastar*), D44 (*selva*, *raiz*). Rows applied: régere, dedúcere, convértere, *Convértere Dómine*, fácies, osténdere, úsquequo, irásci, subsannáre, contradíctio, dux, iter, conspéctus, radix, macéria, destrúere, silva, depáscere, respícere, visitáre, perfícere, déxtera, fílius hóminis, confirmáre, *Ab increpatióne*, vultus, períre, fíeri, discédere, vivificáre, invocáre, poténtia, salvum fácere. Hard readings: 79:6 *in lácrimis in mensúra*; 79:7 *in contradictiónem*; 79:11 *arbústa*; 79:14 *singuláris ferus*; 79:17 the gender of *incénsa … suffóssa* and the subject of *períbunt*.

Hard pass. Soft flags: 79:14 rhyme at both cadences (*devastou … pastou*) — fixed by the Latin's verb-first order; 79:2 second colon +3 — *como ovelha* without the article (+2 left); 79:17 first colon +3 — *a fogo* for *pelo fogo*. Accepted: 79:2b first colon +5 (heuristic counts no elision; *estais sentado* needs the auxiliary), 79:15 second colon -3 (the Latin's proparoxytones), 79:16 first colon +3 (*aperfeiçoai aquela que* — the row's verb and the Latin's relative).
claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. Three minors, no major. Two taken (79:6, 79:11); 79:17 asked no change.

outcomes.remark: *in lácrimis* made the object; keep the preposition
outcomes.reason: *e nos dareis de beber em lágrimas* — *dar de beber* is *potum dare*, and *em* keeps the Latin's openness.

outcomes.remark: feminine singular settles the Latin's gender/number; acceptable, note the reason
outcomes.reason: he asks no change; the reason (the Greek's feminine singular) is in the decision.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context. Ten remarks on nine verses; best line 79:4 (the refrain), worst 79:17. Seven taken (grammar and order), 79:9 refused (D43), 79:17 refused, 79:18 kept as an option.

outcomes.reason: D43 settled *transférre → transportar* and refused *trasladar* as a word for relics; one row across the psalter.

outcomes.remark: *à vista dela* heard as 'in cash', bureaucratic; *diante dela*
*e encheu* has no subject; *e ela encheu*
*a fera solitária a pastou*; *e pastou-a a fera solitária*
colon at the mark so the plural begins a new thought
outcomes.reason: it cuts the participles off from *perecerão* as a sentence of their own, closing what the Latin runs on; the number clash is the Latin's.
the *fíeri* row (*Seja* for jussive *Fiat*, 118:173 held twice against the same request); *Esteja* makes it a state.

outcomes.remark: *de vós, vós* stammer; drop the second *vós*
outcomes.reason: taken in substance by reordering (*E de vós não nos afastamos, vós nos vivificareis*); his clitic-first *nos vivificareis* is not written Portuguese.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, Portuguese only. Most readings are the Latin's own; three fixed (79:10, 79:11, 79:13).

outcomes.reason: the Latin's name, singular as the Latin's *ovem*; nothing to add without explaining.
the sense ruled for (D25's exception); *fazei-nos voltar* is option 2.
D43; *dos exércitos* option, flagged for Gustavo there.

outcomes.remark: heard as a statement until the question mark; *por medida* heard as limited
outcomes.reason: both are the Latin's: its question mark comes at the end too, and *in mensúra* is open.

outcomes.remark: heard as apposition 'its branches were the cedars'

outcomes.reason: the reorder moves the pronoun away from *cerca*; *vindimar* kept (the Latin's one word), *colhem as uvas* option.
D43 (*depáscere → pastar*), the same double hearing as 48:15; *devorou-a* option.

outcomes.remark: *e sobre o filho do homem* a verbless fragment; heard as Christ
outcomes.reason: the Latin's ellipsis (DRB keeps it) and the Latin's phrase; nothing supplied.

outcomes.remark: no noun for *Queimada*; subject of *perecerão* unheard
outcomes.reason: the Latin's; the vine is two verses back in both languages.

outcomes.remark: present *afastamos* may sound boastful; link to *vivificareis* unclear

outcomes.reason: three growth words need three words; concrete images stay (rule 5).

audit.note: v2: 79:5 *estareis irado*; 79:6 *dar de beber em lágrimas*; 79:7 article dropped; 79:10 *diante dela*, *ela* named; 79:11 *o seu arvoredo cobriu*; 79:13 subject before verb; 79:14 *e pastou-a a fera solitária*; 79:19 *E de vós não nos afastamos*. The refrain untouched.

Draft 2: hard pass, no rhyme flag. New length flags accepted: 79:5 second colon +4 (*estareis irado* for *vos irareis*; the counter elides nothing, and the stylist asked for it), 79:10 +3 (*ela* named), 79:11 second colon +5 (the gapped *cobriu* supplied; it is what makes the colon heard rightly).
Gate on draft 2 — claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. No remarks: clean. He names the supplied *cobriu* (79:11) as ellipsis supply, not added content.
site check: the v2 reorder of 79:19 had written *não nos afastamos* as plain text, leaving decision *discedimus* with no slot; the slot is restored (*E de vós {discedimus}*), same text.
